name: Darius
title: king of the Persians
what: He inherits an empire and spends his reign enlarging it. When word comes that Sardis has been burnt he makes no account of the Ionians — they are subjects and cannot escape — but has to ask who the Athenians are, which is the measure of how small a thing Athens is to him in 498. Then he shoots an arrow into the sky and sets a servant to remind him at every dinner. Everything in this prologue follows from that dinner order: two expeditions, six hundred ships, and a war his son finishes.

name: Mardonios
title: son of Gobryas
what: Young, lately married to the king's daughter, and given the whole war in 492 when Darius removes every other commander. He brings army and fleet to Kilikia, boards a ship himself, and loses three hundred ships at Athos and a great many men to the Brygians in one season. He is wounded, subdues the Brygians anyway, and takes the army home without reaching Greece. He returns in 480 under Xerxes and dies at Plataia.

name: Aristagoras
title: tyrant of Miletos
what: He sails from Miletos to ask Athens for help and carries the assembly — twenty ships, and five more from Eretria. What follows is the raid that burns Sardis by accident, from a reed roof, and with it the temple of Hybebe. Herodotus calls those twenty ships the beginning of evils for Greeks and barbarians alike.
